name: Braaibroodjies
summary: Cheese, tomato and onion toasties with a layer of chutney, buttered on the outside and toasted in a hinged grid over gentle coals until golden and oozing.
about: The braaibroodjie is South Africa's own toasted sandwich and, for many families, the best part of the braai. White bread, cheddar, tomato, onion and chutney are the classic filling; buttering the outside of the bread is the trick that gives it its crisp, golden crust. They go on the coals once the meat comes off.
steps: Butter every slice of bread thinly on one side. Lay 8 slices buttered-side down on a board and spread each with 1 tbsp chutney.
Top the chutney with half the cheese, then the tomato and onion slices, a pinch of salt and pepper, and the rest of the cheese, keeping the filling just inside the crusts.
Close each sandwich with a second slice, buttered-side up, press down gently and pack them snugly into a hinged braai grid. Close the grid firmly.

Braai over low coals, the heat you can hold your hand over for 8 to 10 seconds, turning every 1 to 2 minutes, for 8 to 10 minutes in all, until both sides are evenly golden and crisp and the cheese has melted.
Cut each braaibroodjie in half diagonally and serve hot.
prepNote: Assemble up to 2 hours ahead and keep covered in the fridge; braai once the meat comes off the coals.
